title: String concatenation
instruction: Create two string variables `first_name` and `last_name`. Concatenate them with a space in between into a new variable `full_name` and print it.
starter_code:
first_name = "Ada"
last_name = "Lovelace"
# Create full_name and print it
solution_code:
first_name = "Ada"
last_name = "Lovelace"
full_name = first_name + " " + last_name
print(full_name)

title: Use an f-string
instruction: You have variables `city` and `population`. Use an f-string to print: "{city} has a population of {population}."
starter_code:
city = "Tokyo"
population = 37_000_000
# Print using an f-string
solution_code:
city = "Tokyo"
population = 37_000_000
print(f"{city} has a population of {population}.")

title: Upper and lower case
instruction: Convert the given `text` to uppercase and print it, then convert it to lowercase and print it on a new line.
starter_code:
text = "PyThOn Is AwEsOmE"
# Convert to uppercase and print, then lowercase and print

test_cases.expected_output:
PYTHON IS AWESOME
python is awesome

title: Check string length
instruction: Print the length of the string `quote` using `len()`. Then check if the word "mind" is in the quote and print the result (True or False).
starter_code:
quote = "The mind is everything. What you think you become."
# Print length, then check if "mind" is in quote
solution_code:
quote = "The mind is everything. What you think you become."
print(len(quote))
print("mind" in quote)
